concept_title: 보랏빛 달밤의 매화 무대, 뱀과 렌
revision_note: V1 (2ac3ad0) rejected by the owner: too many borders. V2 (73a2823) merged the sky, both lattice doors and the moon/cloud layer into one back plate, shrank the clear rim 2.5 -> 1.0 mm and rendered clear acrylic see-through in the assembly preview. V3 (657a484) recomposed the scene but the owner prefers V2 ("v2가 낫다고 한거야"). V4 (a2a83cd) = V2 plus two owner requests: the blossom tree printed diagonally into the back panel and Len "seated" by cropping her raster at the seat line. V5 = the owner's V4 feedback ("거슬림, 그리고 벛곷나무도 별도 에셋으로 빼, + 나무는 대각선 배치하라고"): (a) the cropped legs bother him, so the whole 84 mm figure is shown again (no crop) and she is seated ON the serpent: the serpent is enlarged 55 -> 70 mm and moved to x=150 so its lower coil rises to her seat line behind her hips, her hanging legs and boots are in front of the coil and her feet reach the base (the bud-guard riser between the legs is the only clear support); (b) the blossom tree is its own cut plate again (5 pieces, 6 slots, 11 closed paths), rotated 25 deg clockwise (86 mm unrotated art height -> 104.3 x 94.2 mm alpha box, larger than V4's printed 80 mm) and placed diagonally across the moon behind the serpent and Len with its tab under the trunk; its canopy contour is a 2.5 mm vector closing of the ink silhouette (clear acrylic between the blossoms, +836 mm2 = 22% of the ink area) so it passes the laser_paths segment gate at the standard 1.0 mm rim (725 of 895 segments). Every rim is 1.0 mm; nothing of Len is cropped.

finished_size_mm.note: 3T: base 3 + tree plate 96.2 (86 mm unrotated art rotated 25 deg, canopy top) = 99.2; the back panel assembles to 94 (3 + 90 art + 1.0 mm rim).

clear_border_rationale: docs/laser-cut-quality.md fixes no rim minimum; its hard limits are the 0.035 mm curve deviation and the 12 mm load-path floor on the buffered silhouette. 1.0 mm is the smallest round offset that still keeps UV ink 0.5 mm inside the cut edge under a 0.5 mm print registration error. V5 keeps 1.0 mm on every plate including the blossom tree: its canopy contour is a smoothed envelope (2.5 mm closing of the ink silhouette, clear acrylic between blossoms) generated through laser_paths.cut_path, so the per-flower detail that forced 1.2 mm in V2/V3 no longer drives the segment count.

overlays.note: left lattice door butted against the sky's left edge, bottoms aligned
right lattice door butted against the sky's right edge, bottoms aligned
moon and both cloud islands registered over the sky as in V2/V4; the blossom tree is no longer printed here (V5: own plate)

pieces.note: V5 owner request: the blossom tree is a cut plate again, placed diagonally like the concept - 86 mm unrotated art (314 ppi source density, 300 ppi cap) rotated 25 deg clockwise at native resolution (alpha box 104.3 x 94.2 mm); the trunk base is the lowest point (x=56 mm of the box), the tab sits under the trunk centre (art-local x=56.5, read 10 mm above the base) and the canopy rises from the lower left (x=0-44 at z=15-20) across the moon to the top at x=61 mm, with the right branch reaching x=104 mm at z=50. Canopy contour = 2.5 mm closing of the ink silhouette (clear acrylic between blossoms) so the 1.0 mm rim passes the segment gate.

V5: enlarged 55 -> 70 mm and moved x 115 -> 150 so its lower coil (top at z=37 mm above the base top) lies behind Len's hips at her seat line (z=32) with its head rising clearly beside her left shoulder; her legs hang in front of the coil. V2 position/scale kept in V2/V4.

V5: the whole 84 mm figure is shown (no crop); the seat line (hips) is 31.5 mm above the art bottom, so she sits on the serpent's coil behind her (row 23) with her legs and boots hanging in front of it and the sword tip 1.0 mm above the base top; the tab is under the hips between the legs and the bud-guard riser is the only clear support between the legs

front_view_policy.note: ORIGIN is a deliberately stacked centre scene (tree across the moon, serpent behind the character): polygon occlusion is by design and overstates visual blocking. Numbers are recorded per piece in validation_report.json; composition acceptance is the vision-checked assembly preview against the supplied concept art. Structural checks (row clearance, overhang, load path, gaps) stay hard.
